text_blocks.snippet: Vertigo, the sensation of spinning or whirling, can be triggered by various factors related to the inner ear, brain, or even certain lifestyle choices. Common triggers include changes in head position, inner ear problems like BPPV or labyrinthitis, and conditions like migraines or dehydration. Additionally, certain medications, head trauma, and even stress can contribute to vertigo episodes.
snippet_highlighted_words: changes in head position, inner ear problems like BPPV or labyrinthitis, and conditions like migraines or dehydration

list.title: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV):
list.snippet: This is the most common cause, triggered by a change in head position, such as rolling over in bed or looking up.

list.title: Inner Ear Infections:
list.snippet: Conditions like labyrinthitis, caused by viral infections, can disrupt the inner ear's balance signals and lead to vertigo.

list.title: Meniere's Disease:
list.snippet: This inner ear disorder causes episodes of vertigo, along with other symptoms like tinnitus (ringing in the ears) and hearing loss.

list.title: Other Inner Ear Problems:
list.snippet: Conditions like vestibular neuritis, acoustic neuroma, and perilymphatic fistula can also cause vertigo.
Central Vertigo: This type of vertigo originates from problems within the brain, such as strokes, brain tumors, or multiple sclerosis.
Vestibular Migraines: Some individuals experience vertigo as part of a migraine headache.
Head Trauma: Injuries to the head can disrupt the balance system and lead to vertigo.
Medications: Certain drugs can cause dizziness as a side effect.
Dehydration: Even mild dehydration can lead to dizziness and vertigo.
Blood Pressure Issues: Both low and high blood pressure can cause dizziness.
Stress and Anxiety: These can trigger vertigo in some individuals.
Certain Foods and Ingredients: Some people may be sensitive to salt, MSG, or alcohol, which can worsen vertigo.
Lack of Sleep: Insufficient sleep can also contribute to dizziness and vertigo.
